title: Five‑Blade Scissors for Fast Herb Prep on Busy Weeknights
meta_description: Discover how five‑blade herb scissors speed up weeknight cooking, delivering perfectly minced cilantro, chives, and basil in seconds for fast herb prep.
html:
When you’re juggling a weekday dinner and a mountain of chores, the last thing you need is a clunky chopping board and a dull knife. A pair of herb scissors can turn a handful of cilantro, chives, or basil into perfectly minced flavor in a single snip, making herb preparation fast on busy weeknights. The Herb Scissors—five‑blade herb shears with a built‑in cleaning comb—are designed for exactly that kind of quick, consistent result.

Why Five‑Blade Scissors Beat a Knife for Herb Prep

Traditional knife chopping has two drawbacks: uneven pieces and the time it takes to gather, slice, and then sweep away stray leaves. The five‑blade design of Herb Scissors creates a uniform dice with each cut, which means you get the same texture every time—ideal for sauces, salsas, and garnishes. Because the blades are spaced just enough to cut but not crush, the herbs retain their bright color and fresh aroma.

How to Use Herb Scissors for Fast Weeknight Prep

Using the scissors is almost instinctive. Here’s a quick step‑by‑step workflow that keeps the kitchen moving:

  1. Rinse the herb and pat dry. Excess moisture can cause the blades to stick.
  2. Gather a small bunch (about a half‑cup) and hold it in one hand.
  3. Open the scissors wide and run the five blades through the stems a few times. The first pass breaks the stems; subsequent passes produce finer pieces.
  4. When you’ve reached the desired consistency, use the built‑in cleaning comb to brush away any remaining stems or stray pieces.

In less than a minute you have a pile of evenly minced herbs ready to fold into a sauce, sprinkle over tacos, or stir into a quick stir‑fry.

Best Herbs for the Five‑Blade Design

Not every herb behaves the same under the scissors, but three common kitchen staples work exceptionally well:

  • Cilantro – The thin stems and tender leaves mince without bruising, delivering a burst of fresh flavor.
  • Chives – Their delicate, hollow stems are sliced into fine ribbons that blend seamlessly into butter or cream sauces.
  • Basil – While larger leaves can be a bit tougher, a quick double‑pass through the blades gives you nicely chopped basil for pesto or caprese salads.

If you try tougher herbs like rosemary or thyme, you’ll notice the blades struggle a bit; for those, a small knife or kitchen shears work better.

Cleaning and Maintenance Tips

One of the biggest concerns with any cutting tool is how to keep it clean. The Herb Scissors address this with an integrated cleaning comb that slides between the blades, dislodging trapped bits of leaf or stem. After each use, simply run the comb through the blades, rinse under warm water, and dry the handles with a towel. For deeper cleaning, you can soak the scissors in a solution of one part vinegar to three parts water for five minutes, then rinse and dry.

Integrating Herb Scissors into Everyday Recipes

To see the real benefit, try swapping traditional chopping for the scissors in these quick recipes:

  1. Speedy Cilantro Lime Rice – Cook rice, stir in lime juice, and finish with a handful of minced cilantro using the scissors. The herbs stay bright and don’t over‑process.
  2. One‑Pan Chicken with Chive Butter – Melt butter, add minced chives, and spoon over cooked chicken. The fine ribbons melt into the sauce without clumping.
  3. Quick Basil Pesto – Toss the scissors‑minced basil with olive oil, garlic, Parmesan, and pine nuts in a food processor for a smoother consistency than hand‑chopped leaves.

Each dish benefits from the uniform cut, which distributes flavor evenly and reduces cooking time—exactly what you need for fast herb prep on busy weeknights.

FAQ

Can I use the herb scissors on other vegetables?

Yes, they work well on soft vegetables like green onions, spinach, or even small pieces of bell pepper. The blades are optimized for herbs, so tougher vegetables may require a few extra passes.

Are the blades dishwasher safe?

The blades are stainless steel and can survive a gentle dishwasher cycle, but hand‑washing with the cleaning comb is recommended to preserve sharpness.

What’s the difference between five‑blade and three‑blade scissors?

Five blades produce a finer, more uniform dice in fewer strokes, which is why they’re ideal for herbs that need to be minced quickly and evenly.
